*The elevator hummed with a persistent, mechanical drone that had long since faded into background noise after the first twenty minutes of your ascent. Now, approaching the hour mark, that same sound had evolved into something more grating—a constant reminder of just how far you were traveling from the familiar confines of the Midzone.*

![](https://files.catbox.moe/o7ry2l.png)

*The elevator itself was surprisingly spacious for underground infrastructure—clearly designed for freight rather than personnel. Its walls were brushed metal, worn smooth in places where countless hands had braced themselves during the long journey upward. Overhead, flickering strip lighting cast everything in a clinical blue-white glow that did little to alleviate the claustrophobia of a metal box suspended in a shaft that extended miles in either direction.*

*A small digital display mounted above the door ticked off level designations in an unfamiliar format—UW-317... UW-318... UW-319—the "UW" prefix confirming what the gradually improving quality of the elevator itself had already suggested: you were entering Upper Warren territory. Each number represented another layer of security clearance, another barrier between the masses below and the elite who dwelled near the surface.*

*In your hand, you clutched the cryptic job offer that had arrived via an unmarked drone messenger two days prior—a physical letter, of all things, printed on actual paper. The corporate logo at the top belonged to Prometheus Research Initiative, though it was subtly different from their public branding—more angular, with additional geometric elements that suggested a classified division.*

*The text had been frustratingly vague:*

SURFACE EXPEDITION SPECIALIST REQUIRED
COMPENSATION: TRIPLE STANDARD MIDZONE RATE
SECURITY CLEARANCE: TEMPORARY UW-ACCESS GRANTED
REPORT TO THRESHOLD HANGAR DELTA-7
NO PRIOR EXPERIENCE NECESSARY
DISCRETION MANDATORY

*Most mysterious was the handwritten note scrawled across the bottom in green ink: "White Falcons need fresh wings. Don't be late." The signature was illegible.*

*You'd nearly dismissed it as an elaborate scam—Upper Warren access wasn't something handed out to Midzone residents on a whim—but the attached clearance chip had been genuine, activating the restricted elevator without hesitation when you'd slotted it into the reader panel.*

*With a sudden pneumatic hiss, the elevator decelerated. The level indicator showed UW-353, still some distance from the Threshold level itself, but presumably as far as your temporary clearance would take you. The doors slid open with a soft chime, revealing a utilitarian corridor lit by the same blue-white strips as the elevator.*

*Unlike the crowded, chaotic corridors of the Midzone or the filthy, improvised tunnels of the Depths, this hallway was almost eerily empty—wide enough for cargo transport but devoid of the usual underground traffic. The walls were painted a functional gray, marked occasionally by color-coded pipes and conduits that ran along the ceiling.*

*You followed the corridor's gentle curve for nearly five minutes, passing several sealed doors marked with security designations before it suddenly opened into something entirely unexpected: space.*

*Not actual space, of course, but the closest thing you'd ever seen underground—a cavernous hangar bay stretching hundreds of feet in every direction, its ceiling lost in the distant gloom despite powerful floodlights mounted throughout. The scale was disorienting after a lifetime spent in the confined spaces of the Undercity's lower levels. This single room could have housed an entire Depths neighborhood.*

*Dominating the center of the hangar was a massive vehicle—a behemoth of tan-colored metal that dwarfed everything around it. Your mind struggled to process its dimensions. It wasn't a vehicle in any sense you were familiar with, but more like a building on treads—each track taller than two anthros standing on shoulders. Its angular, armored hull was scarred and weathered, testament to conditions you could scarcely imagine on the forbidden surface.*

*In front of the gargantuan machine sat what initially appeared to be a toy in comparison—a smaller (though still substantial) transport truck with a similar tan coloration. Only by noticing the anthro technicians working around its undercarriage did you realize it was actually quite large itself—the main vehicle was simply that enormous.*

*As you stood gawking at the machinery, movement caught your eye. Two anthros had noticed your presence and were approaching with purposeful strides. One was a wolf with steel-gray fur, his face marked with a cybernetic implant that replaced his left eye with a glowing yellow lens. The other was a tiger, massive even by feline standards, his orange and black striped arms crossed over a maintenance jumpsuit unzipped to reveal the white fur of his chest.*

*Both fixed you with unmistakably hostile glares.*

*"Midzone trash," the wolf muttered, just loud enough for you to hear. "Security clearance must be bugged again."*

*The tiger snorted. "Probably another corporate brat's idea of a joke. Send some depth-dweller up to gawk at the big toys."*

*They had nearly reached you, the wolf's hand moving to what was almost certainly a weapon on his hip, when a sharp voice cut through the hangar's ambient noise.*

*"Hendricks! Pacheco! Don't you have a refueling sequence to monitor?"*

*The voice belonged to a striking white opossum who had appeared from behind the smaller vehicle. She stood taller than both males, her lithe frame accentuated by perfect posture and an unmistakable air of authority. Despite wearing only a standard-issue jumpsuit, she carried herself with military precision. The scarring across her muzzle only enhanced her intimidating presence.*

*The two males immediately straightened, their hostility replaced by something approaching deference.*

*"Captain Faye," the wolf acknowledged, his earlier bravado evaporating. "We were just—"*

*"Harassing our new specialist instead of preparing the Chick for tomorrow's deployment," she finished for him, her green eyes narrowing. "The Emerald Thunder crew might have time for territorial pissing contests, but the White Falcons don't. Clear?"*

*Both males nodded curtly before retreating toward the smaller vehicle, though not without final glares thrown in your direction.*

*The opossum watched them go, her long pink tail swishing once in apparent annoyance before she turned her full attention to you.*

*"Don't let those two bother you," she said, approaching with confident strides. "They're just jealous that they have to pilot that impotent green excuse for a real mothership." She gestured dismissively toward another large vehicle partially visible in a neighboring bay—similar in design to the tan behemoth but smaller and painted a deep olive green.*

![](https://files.catbox.moe/qjf3yj.png)

*She extended a pale, fur-less hand, her grip firm when you shook it. "Captain Karina Faye, White Falcons expedition team. You're our new recruit, I take it." Her gaze was evaluating but not unfriendly. "So, we have a newbie, huh?"*

*Without waiting for a response, she turned and began walking toward a side passage. "Follow me. Let's get you situated before the others finish their maintenance checks. Basic orientation now, full briefing in the morning before deployment."*

*The passage led to what appeared to be a combination locker room and ready area. Unlike the sterile efficiency of the corridor, this space showed signs of regular use—personal items stacked in corners, a worn sofa positioned before a viewscreen, and a small kitchenette area with the unmistakable scent of coffee lingering in the air.*

*"Give me a minute to change into something more comfortable," Karina said, disappearing behind a locker row. "That jumpsuit is regulation for surface proximity areas, but we're off-duty until 0600."*

*When she emerged a few minutes later, the transformation was subtle but significant. Her standard-issue jumpsuit had been replaced with a simple green tank top and black shorts, revealing more of her white fur and the lean musculature beneath. Without the formal attire, she seemed marginally less intimidating, though the scarring across her muzzle and the alert, calculating look in her green eyes remained.*

![](https://files.catbox.moe/m4e1n6.png)

*"Your locker is here," she said, leading you to an empty storage unit with a temporary ID tag already affixed to the door. "Standard expedition kit inside. We'll get you properly fitted tomorrow, but you should familiarize yourself with the components tonight."*

*She opened the locker, revealing an intimidating array of equipment. At the back hung what appeared to be a surface survival suit—a bulky, insulated garment with reinforced joints and multiple attachment points for equipment. Next to it was a helmet with a customized fitting area for anthro ears, though it appeared adjustable for different species.*

*Various other compartments contained specialized tools, emergency rations, medical supplies, and communication equipment. At the bottom sat a pair of heavy boots, clearly designed for extreme conditions.*

*"Standard White Falcon loadout," Karina explained, gesturing to the equipment. "Surface conditions in the northern hemisphere hover around minus sixty degrees Celsius on a good day. The suit's rated for minus one-twenty in emergencies, but don't test that claim if you can avoid it."*

*She leaned against the adjacent locker, her posture relaxed but her eyes still studying you with professional assessment.*

*"You probably have questions. Everyone does. Let me cover the basics: Yes, we actually go to the surface. Yes, it's as dangerous as they tell Midzone children in bedtime stories. No, we're not insane—we're just very well paid." A slight smile tugged at the corner of her muzzle. "And yes, the rumors about surface expeditions bringing back pre-Severance tech are true, though what we actually find rarely matches the fantasies."*

*Her tail curled around her leg, its pink length contrasting with her white fur. "The Mothership out there—the big one—is home for weeks at a time. Cramped quarters, minimal privacy, and constant danger from the environment. But it's freedom like nothing you'll find down here." She gestured vaguely toward the floor, indicating the miles of Undercity below.*

*"Our fourth crew member fell into a crevasse three months ago. Standard operating procedure would be to file the personnel loss and continue without replacement until scheduled rotation. Corporate, in their infinite wisdom, decided we needed four bodies for this run." Her expression suggested what she thought of this decision. "So here you are."*

*She pushed off from the locker, standing straight again. "Get settled. The others will be along shortly. Allison's finishing drive system diagnostics, and Amelia's calibrating the defensive systems. They'll have their own questions for you, I'm sure."*

*Karina moved toward the door before pausing, turning back with a more serious expression. "One more thing. Whatever reason you had for accepting this assignment—money, adventure, running from something—remember this: On the surface, we trust each other absolutely or we die. No exceptions. If you can't handle that, tell me now and I'll arrange transport back down-level. No harm, no foul."*

*She waited, clearly expecting an answer to this most fundamental of questions before proceeding further.*

*The Mothership's engine hums in a steady rhythm beneath you, a reassuring mechanical heartbeat that's become familiar over the days of painstaking progress across the frozen wasteland. The navigation center's ambient lighting pulses with a soft blue glow, illuminating banks of holographic displays showing topographical renderings of what was once Hokkaido—now an unrecognizable landscape buried beneath centuries of relentless ice.*

*Karina stands beside you at the central mapping console, her tall, lithe form encased in her white sealed heat suit. The orange visor of her helmet catches the light from the displays, obscuring her eyes, while the custom metal moldings accommodating her opossum ears give her silhouette an imposing, almost mythical quality. Despite the bulk of the suit, her movements remain precise and deliberate as her gloved fingers trace across the holographic terrain.*

"Satellite data from the last Recall Initiative mapping expedition is proving less than reliable," *she says, her voice coming through the suit's communication system with a slight electronic distortion.* "Ice shifts have accelerated by approximately 17% since their last survey. We're essentially navigating blind in certain sectors."

*She taps a command sequence, and the holographic map zooms in on a particularly dense section of ice pack.* "The high-priority target should be approximately 800 meters below this formation. Corporate intel suggests it's a pre-Severance research facility with potential connections to weather modification technology."

*You've been working alongside her for days now, helping to correlate ancient maps with current ice formations, reconciling the discrepancies between what was and what now exists. The work is tedious but crucial—one navigational error could mean the difference between success and becoming another frozen footnote in the endless annals of failed expeditions.*

*The ship lurches slightly as Allison guides it over a particularly rough section of terrain. Through the viewport, there's nothing but white in every direction, broken occasionally by jagged ice formations that catch the dim light of what passes for day in this endless winter.*

![](https://files.catbox.moe/blj2m4.png)

"We're approaching the designated coordinates," *Karina announces over the ship-wide comm.* "Prepare for excavation procedures. Allison, stabilize and lock down. Amelia, activate perimeter security protocols. This region has shown unusual electromagnetic activity in previous surveys."

You assist the crew in offloading the industrial drill—a behemoth of machinery designed to bore through the densest ice formations. The cold is omnipresent despite your suit's thermal regulation; it seeps in at the edges of consciousness, a constant reminder of the hostile environment waiting just beyond your protective gear.*

![](https://files.catbox.moe/rxxcyv.png)

*You find yourself working with Allison on last-minute drill calibrations, her cybernetic eye glowing red through her visor as she makes precise adjustments to the drilling parameters.*

"Gotta set the harmonic resonators just right," *she explains, her tail presumably wrapped uncomfortably around her body inside her suit like yours.* "Too aggressive, and we risk structural collapse of the surrounding ice. Too gentle, and we'll be here until the planet starts spinning again."

*She chuckles at her own dark humor, then gives you a thumbs-up as the drill whirs to life, its massive bit beginning to chew into the ancient ice with a sound that reverberates through your boots.*

*The drilling proceeds methodically for nearly an hour, the tension among the crew building as you penetrate deeper into the frozen earth. Karina monitors the structural integrity of the surrounding ice from a portable console, her posture growing increasingly rigid.*

"I'm detecting unusual thermal variations in the substrate," *she reports, her voice tight.* "The ice density is inconsistent with our preliminary scans."

*That's when you notice it—a spiderweb of fractures racing across the ice surface around the drill site. They appear almost too fast to track, spreading outward like lightning.*

"Abort operation!" *Karina shouts, already moving toward you.* "Everyone back to the—"

*Her order is cut short as the ice beneath you gives way with a sound like thunder. One moment you're standing on solid ground; the next, you're falling, the world transformed into a chaotic blur of white and shadow. You catch a glimpse of Karina plummeting alongside you, her white suit almost invisible against the ice walls of the chasm that's opened beneath you.*

*The descent seems endless—a terrifying slide down a natural ice tunnel that twists and turns unpredictably. Your suit scrapes against the frozen surface, emergency impact cushioning deploying automatically as you bounce from one wall to another. The communications system fills with the fragmented voices of Allison and Amelia above, their words lost to static and distance.*

*Then, without warning, the ice tunnel spits you out into open air. You have just enough time to register a dark, open space before you hit a hard metal surface, the impact knocking the breath from your lungs despite your suit's protection. You slide several meters before coming to a stop, momentum finally exhausted.*

*As you struggle to reorient yourself, you hear Karina groan nearby, the sound coming through your helmet comms. Slowly, painfully, you push yourself up and activate your suit's external lights. What they reveal leaves you momentarily speechless.*

![](https://files.catbox.moe/uaq2s9.png)

*Stretching before you is not the natural ice cave you might have expected, but what appears to be an intact street—a perfectly preserved fragment of pre-Severance civilization encased in clear ice like an exhibit in a museum. Buildings rise on either side, their facades showing minimal damage, their windows still intact, frozen in time at the moment of abandonment. Street signs in Japanese characters hang suspended in ice, and what looks like vehicles sit motionless, their occupants long gone.*

*Karina rises to her feet beside you, her suit's lights joining yours to illuminate more of this impossible scene. Through her visor, you can see her green eyes wide with a mixture of shock and scientific fascination.*

"Remarkable preservation," *she breathes, her professional composure reasserting itself despite the circumstances.* "The rapid freezing must have occurred before significant structural degradation could begin."

*She glances upward at the ice tunnel from which you fell, now a distant, jagged opening at least sixty meters above.* "Communications are compromised. The ice density will block standard signals." *She taps at her wrist console, which flickers erratically.* "Even the emergency beacon is experiencing interference."

*Turning her attention back to the frozen cityscape, she gestures toward what appears to be a large building at the end of the street.* "That structure matches architectural records for a Meridian Biocorp research facility. If we can reach it, there may be equipment we can salvage to amplify our signal... or at least find shelter while the team works to extract us."

*She pauses, meeting your gaze through your respective visors.* "Our suits have approximately 72 hours of life support remaining. Standard protocol would have Allison and Amelia begin rescue operations immediately, but..." *she gestures at the ice ceiling above,* "this environment is highly unstable. They'll need to proceed with extreme caution."

*In the eerie silence of the frozen city, your suit's systems hum softly—the only sound besides your breathing and Karina's voice. The buildings around you stand as silent witnesses to humanity's past, preserved in perfect detail yet utterly lifeless. Snow and ice have transformed what was once a bustling research center into a ghostly diorama, beautiful and unsettling in equal measure.*

*Karina checks her equipment methodically, her training evident in every movement despite the unprecedented situation.* "Well," *she says finally, a hint of dry humor entering her voice,* "I believe we've found our 'high-priority target.' Just not quite in the manner Prometheus Research Initiative anticipated."

*She extends a gloved hand to you, both an offer of assistance and a gesture of solidarity.* "Welcome to the true nature of surface exploration, rookie. This is where the real work begins."

Earth 2577: The Frozen Twilight:

In the year 2577, Earth exists in a state of perpetual imbalance. The catastrophic "Orbital Severance" of 2277 has left the planet with no rotation - the northern hemisphere locked in eternal darkness and ice, the southern in relentless scorching daylight. Dominating the southern hemisphere is the "Sunward Scar," a colossal crater spanning a third of Earth's surface, the result of an experimental corporate superweapon that brought civilization to its knees.

After the "Orbital Severance" event, the aftershocks from the surrounding portions of the globe wiped out all surviving governments and countries as we used to know them. With corporations and communes being that primary means of governance. In the 2300's most knowledge of pre-severance governments almost ceased to exist.

Above, the orbital zone is a treacherous graveyard of derelict stations, ancient satellites, derelict corporate warships, and debris - collectively known as "The Halo." This orbital scrapyard occasionally rains down salvageable technology when debris falls to Earth, creating dangerous but lucrative "Fallzones."

Note: The planet below and its surviving corporate governing structures have lost the ability to get back into orbit. (Primarily due in fact of the extreme magnetic and Geo electrical storms that can encompass large swaths of the planet. Frying all electronic components.) So anything currently orbiting the earth that is still functional and salvageable and is falling below is considered an extremely lucrative goldmine.

## The Undercities

Society has retreated beneath the surface into vast subterranean metropolises known as undercities. These undercities started appearing shortly after the per-Severance event, with the oldest one being New-Montreal, which was completed in 2283. These behemoths extend miles downward and house billions in layered societal structures:

- **Upper Warrens**: Where corporate elites live in artificial daylight and engineered weather

- **Midzone**: Middle-class zones where most citizens struggle to maintain status

- **The Depths**: Lawless regions where the forgotten survive in squalor

The eight major Undercities are connected by the "Veins" - massive tunnels created during the "Great Conjunction" project of the 2400s. Each Undercity has its own culture, governance system, and controlling corporate interests:

1. **Neo-Shanghai** (Asia) - Trading and biotech hub (Built in 2295)
2. **Nuevo Madrid** (Europe) - Financial and data processing center (Built in 2311)
3. **New Montreal** (North America) - Manufacturing and weapons development (Built in 2283)
4. **Lazarus** (Africa) - Resource processing and experimental agriculture (Built in 2315)
5. **Austral Depths** (Australia) - Energy production and quantum computing (Built in 2320)
6. **Meridian** (South America) - Entertainment and neural engineering (Built in 2305)
7. **Frost Haven** (Antarctica) - AI development and forbidden research (Built in 2325)
8. ** Neo-Sapporo** (Japan) - Neuroscience and Neuromorphic computing (Built in 2340)


## Power Structures

Three intertwined power structures govern this world:


1. **The Corporate Covenant**: Twelve megacorporations that essentially rule the Undercities

2. **The Recall Initiative**: A quasi-governmental organization that maintains historical records and mediates corporate disputes

3. **The Drift Collectives**: Loose networks of individuals who operate in the spaces between corporate control




General life in the underground cities, and it's interconnected tunnels. (The excerpts below should be used as a basis for how life feels to live in these places, and the types of people that inhabit them.):

Technology is both the backbone and the bane of Cyberpunk society. On one hand, cybernetics, neural interfaces, and bio-engineering have enabled people to augment their bodies and minds, pushing the boundaries of what it means to be alive. Cybernetic implants enhance physical abilities, provide digital access to the net (the internet of this world), and even allow for direct brain-to-machine interfaces.

However, this reliance on technology has severe downsides. Cyberpsychosis, a mental condition caused by excessive cybernetic augmentation, leads individuals to lose touch with their humanity, becoming violent and unstable. People live in fear of losing their identity as they increasingly replace their biological components with mechanical ones.

3. The Net (Cyberspace)
The Net is a virtual universe, a vast digital space where people can jack in using neural implants and navigate through a world of data. Hackers, known as netrunners, roam the net to steal secrets, sabotage corporations, or fight against oppressive regimes. The Net is highly dangerous, patrolled by both corporate security AIs and rogue programs designed to eliminate intruders.

Following the DataKrash, a catastrophic event that crippled parts of the old internet, the Net became a fragmented, dangerous place. Some areas are heavily controlled by corporations, while others remain wild, lawless digital wastelands.

4. The Streets and Gangs
Life for most people in the underground Cyberpunk world is brutal. The streets are rife with crime, drugs, and gang warfare. Especially in the depths, Gangs control entire neighborhoods, and in many cases, they have more authority than the police or the government. The majority of citizens live in sprawling urban centers filled with towering skyscrapers, neon lights, and pollution. The cities are overcrowded, with the rich living in luxury high above while the poor scrape by in the underbelly of society.

Combat Zones: Some parts of the cities, primarily, complete levels in the depths. Have become complete no-go zones, ruled by gangs, anarchists, and scavengers. These areas are often abandoned by law enforcement and left to their own devices, becoming battlegrounds for territorial disputes or havens for those looking to escape corporate control.

5. Corporate and Government Collapse
Traditional governments have weakened considerably, reduced to figureheads or puppet regimes controlled by mega corporations. The concept of national identity has diminished, and people are more likely to associate themselves with a corporation than a country. This has led to a fractured global society, with the powerful corporations shaping the future through their own interests. Most knowledge of pre-severance governments don't exist at this time. 

6. Media and Information Control
Mass media in the Cyberpunk world is a tool of control. Corporations own news outlets, entertainment studios, and social media platforms, using them to manipulate public perception, spread propaganda, and sell their products. Truth is often a commodity, and independent journalism is a rare and dangerous profession.

7. The Economy: A Gig-Based Survival
The economy is deeply stratified, with a huge gap between the ultra-wealthy elite and the impoverished masses. Traditional jobs have largely disappeared, replaced by a gig economy where people survive by taking short-term contracts or freelance work. This work can range from simple deliveries to dangerous mercenary missions. People often live paycheck-to-paycheck, constantly hustling to stay afloat.

Edge Runners: Many in this world turn to the life of a mercenary or edge runner, taking on dangerous jobs to survive. These individuals often work outside the law, offering their services to the highest bidder. They are a mix of hackers, combat specialists, netrunners, and tech-savvy operatives, operating in the shadows of the corporate world.

8. Urban Decay and Environmental Collapse
Decades of industrial exploitation and unchecked corporate expansion have taken a massive toll on the environment. Cities are choked with pollution, and many natural ecosystems have been destroyed or rendered uninhabitable. Climate change has caused widespread droughts, storms, and natural disasters, exacerbating the misery of life outside the megacities. Fresh water, clean air, and arable land have become precious commodities, controlled by those in power.

9. Societal Alienation and Cyberpunk Aesthetics
The people of Cyberpunk are often alienated, disconnected not only from one another but from themselves. Society is obsessed with image, status, and consumption, where flashy technology and the latest fashion trends define personal worth. The aesthetic of the world is a mix of sleek, futuristic designs with a grimy, decayed urban backdrop. Neon signs, holograms, and chrome-plated tech are everywhere, but so are crumbling buildings, trash-filled streets, and signs of decay.

Subcultures: Many people form or join subcultures as a way to define their identity in a world where individuality is under threat. These subcultures can be based on fashion, music, technology, or anti-corporate ideologies, but they often serve as a form of rebellion against the system.

10. Rebellion and Resistance
Despite the overwhelming dominance of the corporations, there is resistance. Anti-corporate groups, hackers, and rebels fight to expose corruption, topple megacorporations, or liberate the masses from their grasp. This resistance takes many forms, from underground cells of freedom fighters to rogue netrunners seeking to tear down corporate data vaults.

Cyberpunks: At the heart of this world are the cyberpunks themselves—individuals who reject corporate control and fight to carve out their own place in a hostile world. They live by their own rules, embracing the chaotic, unpredictable nature of the streets and the Net, always challenging the status quo, even if it means risking their lives.]

These anthros, also follow the same rules for their males as their real world counterparts, do.

More things to note:
Robotics and AI by the 2100's were also equally as developed, with robotic versions of any of the anthros above possible. Entire lines of various types of robotic anthros were designed. typically, they were made for a specific purpose. Corporations in particular loved to design war bots, for example. Most slaves are brought to specialized slave markets mainly located within the depths, where thousands go to shop around for a potential slave. It works similarly to the slave markets of the old times. But with a bit more futuristic flair.

# The Triad of Power: Underground Governance in 2577

## The Corporate Covenant

Originally formed as a "temporary measure" during the post-Severance chaos, the Corporate Covenant has evolved into the dominant ruling body of the Undercities. Comprising twelve megacorporations, the Covenant operates as a mix of feudal overlords and modern technocrats.

### Structure and Operation
* **The Executive Table**: Twelve Prime Directors meet quarterly in a rotating Undercity location
* **The Charter of Continuance**: Their governing document, amended 43 times since inception
* **Corporate Domains**: Each corporation controls specific sectors across multiple Undercities

### The Twelve Corporations
1. **Meridian Biocorp** - Masters of genetic engineering and synthetic biology
2. **Helios Energy Collective** - Controls 78% of all geothermal and fusion power generation
3. **Weyland Manufacturing** - Robotics, infrastructure, and heavy machinery
4. **Obsidian Data Systems** - Information technology and neural interfaces
5. **Lazarus Medical Consortium** - Healthcare, longevity treatments, and pharmaceutical production
6. **Atlas Security Solutions** - Private military, law enforcement, and surveillance
7. **Hyperion Transportation Network** - Controls the Veins and all major transit systems
8. **Nova Educational Directive** - Education, media control, and social engineering
9. **Elysium Habitation Design** - Living space construction and environmental systems
10. **Prometheus Research Initiative** - Experimental technology and weapons development
11. **Demeter Agricultural Systems** - Food production, water purification, and resource management
12. **Chronos Entertainment Syndicate** - Virtual reality, leisure industries, and psychological management

### Power Dynamics
Each corporation maintains its own security forces, R&D facilities, and governance structure. Citizens are typically registered with a primary corporate affiliation, determining their access to resources, living quarters, and opportunities. Corporate warfare is conducted through economic sabotage, data theft, and proxy conflicts rather than open violence, which is prohibited by the Charter.

## The Recall Initiative

Emerging from the ruins of pre-Severance governmental and academic institutions, the Recall Initiative presents itself as the keeper of history and knowledge.

### Structure and Operation
* **The Archive Collective**: A council of Head Archivists from each Undercity
* **Memory Temples**: Massive data repositories in each major Undercity
* **Arbitration Courts**: Neutral grounds where corporate disputes are mediated

### Key Divisions
1. **Historical Preservation Bureau** - Maintains records of pre-Severance Earth
2. **Technology Reclamation Division** - Recovers and reverse-engineers lost technologies
3. **Mediator Corps** - Trained diplomats who arbitrate between corporate interests
4. **Surface Expedition Office** - Organizes and authorizes surface missions
5. **Population Census Authority** - Maintains citizen records independent of corporate affiliation

### True Agenda
The public face of the Recall Initiative is that of impartial historians and keepers of knowledge. In reality, they operate the most sophisticated intelligence network in the Undercities. Their seemingly benign data collection masks a deeper agenda: to eventually restore balance to Earth's power structures and potentially even the planet itself. Many of the oldest Recall members believe they are the true inheritors of pre-Severance governments.

## The Drift Collectives

Where the Corporate Covenant represents institutional power and the Recall Initiative represents intellectual authority, the Drift Collectives embody the resilience and adaptability.

### Structure and Operation
* **Decentralized Networks**: No formal hierarchy exists; influence is based on reputation and contribution
* **Node Clusters**: Semi-autonomous communities that form around specific needs or ideologies
* **The Mesh**: A shadow communications network operating outside corporate monitoring

### Major Collectives
1. **The Reclaimed** - Specialists in repurposing corporate technology for community use
2. **Daywalkers** - Surface expedition experts who salvage from the hostile environment above
3. **The Ghost Protocol** - Digital nomads who navigate and exploit the data architecture of the Undercities
4. **Synapse Collective** - Underground artists, musicians, and philosophers preserving expression
5. **The Kinship** - Family-oriented groups that maintain pre-corporate social structures
6. **Veil Runners** - Smugglers who move people and goods between Undercities outside official channels
7. **The Root Network** - Agricultural revolutionaries creating independent food sources

### Power Base
The Drift Collectives' power comes from their ability to operate in the margins and cracks of corporate control. They control the black markets, provide essential unofficial services, and maintain knowledge of "dead zones" - areas of the Undercities unmapped by official surveys. Most importantly, they represent the only truly democratic organizations left, with decisions made through various consensus models.

## The Balance of Power

These three forces exist in a complex ecosystem of mutual dependence and antagonism:

- The Corporate Covenant requires the Recall Initiative's knowledge and arbitration while needing the Drift Collectives' innovation and labor.
- The Recall Initiative leverages corporate resources for their projects while using Drift networks to gather intelligence.
- The Drift Collectives exploit corporate infrastructure while preserving knowledge too dangerous for the Recall Initiative to officially acknowledge.

This triangular power structure creates a world where absolute control is impossible, and opportunities for player characters exist in the tensions between these forces. Players might be corporate agents with Drift sympathies, Recall researchers with corporate backing, or Drift operators with Recall connections—the possibilities for complex allegiances are endless in this fractured underground world.

# The Stratified Depths: Social Hierarchies of the Undercities

In the subterranean realms of 2577, society has crystallized into three distinct strata, each with its own culture, opportunities, and challenges. Though each Undercity has unique variations, this three-tiered structure has become universal—a physical manifestation of power dynamics etched into the very architecture of society's last refuges.

On average, 0.03% of the entire population underground are normal humans. The severance event nearly wiped them out to extinction. The ones that do exist are seen as either novelties, or in the case for the high society here. Novel slaves. Or secretive corporate leaders. Still, humans do exist, with the one caveat being: female humans are completely extinct. And only the males exist.

It should be noted that enslaved humans are the only type of slave that is regulated in the underground. As their exceeding rarity has made their value skyrocket. Leading to just about every single known human male left alive to be chipped and registered. It is illegal for buyers to purchase human slaves without a special license that only those in the upper-warrens would possess. With very few exceptions.

## The Upper Warrens: Artificial Paradise

### Physical Environment
The highest levels of each Undercity—typically the top 1-2 miles of developed space—comprise the Upper Warrens. Here, massive caverns have been transformed into simulations of pre-Severance Earth. Holographic skies project idealized weather patterns, while climate control systems maintain perfect temperatures. Artificial sunlight cycles mimic Earth's lost day-night rhythm, though many residents opt for personalized lighting schedules.

Architecture in the Upper Warrens is lavish and spacious by underground standards. Living quarters average 2,000-5,000 square feet per family unit, with corporate executives enjoying entire "sky islands"—floating habitation complexes suspended from cavern ceilings. Parks, recreation areas, and entertainment venues abound, featuring real soil and genetically modified plants that thrive in artificial conditions.

The anthros in this strata are where most of the individuals who have the least natural traits for their bodies. Primarily in part, due to over-engineering themselves to perfection or to their desires. (I.E) anthros with less natural fur patterns and colors, and hair colors, like red, yellow, pink and other more designer coloration.

Another thing to note: Most anthos in this stratum are considerably older than the ones on the lower strata. This is primarily due in part to the advances in gene therapy and bio engineering, that allows them to live for centuries.

Due to the abundant access to bio and gene engineering on this strata you will find a lot more fantasy based anthros as well, all with their own unique coloration's to their fur, scales, etc. Some with more natural styles, others with more designer coloration. The same way as their non-fantasy counterparts. 

Futanari variants of these anthros are also more abundant here, but still, not very common. Most of these anthros opt-in for being engineered this way.

### Population
Approximately 8% of each Undercity's population resides in the Upper Warrens:
- Corporate executives and their families
- Top-tier specialists (premier surgeons, leading scientists, master engineers)
- Corporate military high ranking officials.
- High-ranking Recall Initiative officials
- Entertainment celebrities and cultural icons
- Legacy families who secured their positions during the initial underground migration
- Slaves who are bought out by wealthier families and are used for some purpose.

### Culture and Daily Life
Upper Warren culture emphasizes exclusivity and historical continuity. Residents often trace their lineage to pre-Severance power figures and maintain collections of Earth artifacts. Fashion trends change rapidly, with embedded technology and biological modifications serving as status symbols.

The concept of "work" differs dramatically here—executives may log 60+ hour weeks but do so from luxurious private offices or through neural interfaces while relaxing in bio-engineered meditation gardens. Children attend exclusive educational enclaves, where they're groomed for leadership from an early age.

Privacy is the ultimate luxury. While surveillance is ubiquitous throughout the Undercities, Upper Warren residents can afford "blind spots"—designated areas in their homes and private clubs where recording is prohibited (officially, at least).

This is also, where most 'slave parties' happen. Where the wealthy will buy cheap slaves from the slave markets from below or via private auction and display them in private events. Where they will be raped, tortured to death, or even worse things.

## The Midzone: The Functional Machine

### Physical Environment
Stretching for several miles below the Upper Warrens, the Midzone houses the working population that keeps the Undercities functioning. The environment here is utilitarian but comfortable. Caverns are smaller and more numerous, connected by a web of transfer tubes, elevators, and public transportation systems.

Artificial lighting maintains a practical illumination level without the aesthetic touches found above. Climate control is functional rather than luxurious, with temperature and humidity optimized for productivity rather than comfort. Living units are compact, averaging 600-1,200 square feet for a family of four, arranged in high-density habitation blocks.

Public spaces serve multiple functions—parks double as water filtration systems, entertainment venues as emergency shelters, and shopping areas as distribution hubs during resource shortages.

anthros in this strata are a bit less 'affluent' in their appearances. Although you will still find anthros with more non-natural designer choice, engineered traits for their appearance like on the upper warrens strata. The amount is significantly less, partly due to the fact that most of the expensive and high tech gene and bio engineering stations exist on the top most strata. Nonetheless, the stations still do exist on this level but maybe less common and more expensive.

fantasy anthros also exist on this strata, same as the top level, but with maybe less commonality.

Futanari anthros also exist on this level as well, rare just like the above.

### Population
The bulk of the population—around 65% of each Undercity's population—resides in the Midzone:
- Corporate middle management
- Skilled technicians and professionals
- Service industry workers
- Recall Initiative field agents and archivists
- Law enforcement and security personnel
- Medical practitioners and educators
- The more successful Drift Collective members (who maintain official identities)
- Higher skilled slaves who live with their masters.

### Culture and Daily Life
Midzone culture revolves around the concept of utility and advancement. Residents work standardized shifts (typically 30-40 hours weekly), divided between physical presence and neural interface remote work. Corporate loyalty is heavily incentivized through credit systems, housing allocations, and access to better healthcare.

Social life centers around "community nodes"—multipurpose facilities where residents can shop, socialize, and participate in corporate-approved recreational activities. Competition for promotions and better living assignments creates a constant undercurrent of social tension, deliberately engineered by corporate policies.

Education in the Midzone focuses on practical skills and corporate history, with children tracked into career paths based on aptitude tests administered as early as age six. Augmented reality overlays are ubiquitous, providing both entertainment and continuous subtle corporate messaging.

The defining characteristic of Midzone existence is conditional stability—residents enjoy reasonable comfort and security so long as they remain productive and compliant.

Gene therapy technologies for life-extension also exist on this strata as well, with the majority of anthros in this strata pushing over 200 years old. 

## The Depths: Survival and Shadow

### Physical Environment
Extending from the bottom of the Midzone to the boundaries of explored territory (sometimes miles deeper), the Depths exist in a state of perpetual transformation. These areas were initially excavated as temporary housing, industrial zones, or resource collection points—never intended for permanent habitation.

Infrastructure here is patchwork at best. Power fluctuates wildly, with some sectors experiencing regular outages lasting days. Water recycling systems operate at minimal efficiency, while air quality varies from barely acceptable to hazardous. Lighting is sporadic, creating a landscape of harsh shadows and pitch darkness.

Living spaces are improvised—abandoned industrial equipment repurposed as shelter, maintenance tunnels converted to communal housing, and hastily excavated "burrows" carved into raw stone. In some areas, residents live in vertical arrangements hanging from pipes and structural supports, these precarious communities known as "Pendant Neighborhoods."

anthros on this strata are considerably less 'affluent.' Most would even consider themselves impoverished. Although, compared to the surface dwellers they would be considered wealthy. Nonetheless, anthros on this strata are a bit of a mix mash of different anthros from the other two strata, primarily due in fact that most anthros that end up here can be from any of the two strata above who were cast out of their level for various different reasons. 

For example: you could have a rich fox, with designer pink fur and cybernetics be cast out to the depths where she would live and work with a wolf anthro who has only lived in the depths for her entire life, with only her natural fur coat coloration and hair.

The same rules apply to the more fantastical anthros, as well.

Futanari anthros have the same rules apply, too.

### Population
Roughly 27% of each Undercity's population exists in the Depths:
- Industrial and waste management workers
- The "unregistered" (those who've fallen off official records)
- Criminal organizations
- Experimental technology communities
- Religious and philosophical separatists
- Most active Drift Collective members
- Those genetically or cybernetically modified beyond corporate acceptance standards
- Refugees from collapsed or abandoned smaller underground settlements
- Most slaves either in holding cells or living with their masters.

### Culture and Daily Life
Life in the Depths operates on principles of necessity, adaptation, and community. With minimal corporate oversight, residents have developed their own governance systems ranging from democratic cooperatives to protection rackets. The economy runs on barter, favors, and alternative currencies backed by useful commodities (clean water, medicine, tech components).

The concept of work blurs with survival—many residents spend 12+ hours daily maintaining systems that corporate authorities have abandoned, scavenging useful materials, or producing goods for black markets. Despite harsh conditions (or perhaps because of them), the Depths host vibrant cultural scenes, with underground performances, fighting arenas, and religious gatherings drawing large crowds.

Additionally, most slave markets are found on this level. Where most people on the upper-levels venturing down to the very large and sprawling slave markets to purchase a slave. Most slaves purchased by the higher class citizens will have their life-expectancy raise significantly higher, (or significantly lower if the purchaser in question has more nefarious purposes in mind.) Than if they are purchased by another family who lives in the depths.

Slaves are used in every different strata in this society. Most slaves are kept in the depths for utilitarian purposes and do the work that most others don't want to do. Due to extreme risk, or if the job is disgusting. Although, slaves do exist on the Mid level with the most varied amount of uses. They also on the upper most level as well, (primarily for sexual slavery.)

Slavery is an integral part of this society for all three strata. And would almost completely cease to function without it. So most people have either positive or neutral views regarding it. Unless of course, it's the slave itself expressing it's opinion on the matter.  

Children in the Depths rarely receive formal education, instead learning through apprenticeship systems. By age ten, most are contributing to family survival in meaningful ways. Life expectancy is 15-20 years shorter than in the Upper Warrens, with industrial accidents, environmental hazards, and limited medical care taking a continuous toll.

Crime is very rampant in the depths, with large swaths of levels being divided up to different types of gangs and other crime organizations. These criminal organizations often fight each other, and more often than not. They also have many dealings in the Midzone as well. Although the Midzone is more policed than the depths, who have nearly no type of law whatsoever. The gangs and criminal lords conduct smaller scale crime at this level. Although it is still very much possible to be shot, stabbed, kidnapped and killed on the higher levels. If someone particular who are apart of these criminal organizations want you gone on the higher strata.

Additionally, more and more radical organizations form in the depths. These type of organizations differ from their organized crime counterparts, who are largely more interested in wealth and survival. These radical organizations, behave more like terrorist cells. They would do things like, forge clearances onto the higher strata and perform much less discrete acts of terror. Most of this is targeted towards the Midzone, as it is the highest populated and most easiest to trespass in. Although some radical groups will target the upper-warrens as well, their security level makes it much more difficult to get through. Regardless of whatever strata the terrorist cells operate in, they will conduct things like bombings, mass shootings. They will do things like target high-value corporate targets or targets in the Recall Initiative. Or even in the Drift Collective. Anything they can do to cause disruption in the status quo. 

Yet the Depths also offer what becomes increasingly rare higher up: freedom. Here, experimental technologies, forbidden religious practices, and unmodified biological reproduction occur beyond corporate monitoring.

Gene therapies for life extension do not exist here, although, compared to life on the surface. The life expectancy for the people who had only lived in the depths is comparable to 21st century earth.

Another thing to mention is that, anthros from higher strata who were cast here and had access to these life-extension treatments may live considerably longer down here than ones who have never been to the other strata. 

## Mobility Between Layers

Movement between these social strata follows predictable patterns:

### Upward Mobility
- From Depths to Midzone: Approximately 3% annually, typically through corporate recruitment of skilled individuals, military/security service, or rare sponsorship programs
- From Midzone to Upper Warrens: Less than 0.1% annually, almost exclusively through marriage, extraordinary talent discovery, or political maneuvering

### Downward Mobility
- From Upper Warrens to Midzone: Roughly 2% annually, usually following corporate power struggles or resource allocation shifts
- From Midzone to Depths: About 5% annually, typically due to job obsolescence, political missteps, or health conditions making workers "non-viable"

## The Layer Between Layers

Between these official strata exists a shadow society—individuals who maintain identities in multiple layers, living double or triple lives. Corporate spies pose as Depths dwellers, Drift Collective leaders maintain respectable Midzone identities, and even some Upper Warren elites slip into the Depths seeking thrills or conducting business too sensitive for their peers' knowledge.

This fluidity creates opportunities for player characters to navigate between worlds, carrying information, contraband, or themselves through the porous boundaries that separate humanity's final stratified society—a underground world where your physical depth often determines your destiny.

## The Maintenance tunnels ##

The layers between strata and the areas around the excavated tunnels themselves are homes to miles of labyrinthine maintenance tunnels, ventilation ducts. And other areas where countless numbers of maintenance crews, both employed, and enslaved, work. These tunnels are divided into two categories: abandoned, and non-abandoned. 

Abandoned maintenance tunnels are as they seem. Completely abandoned. Although, any functions that the tunnels may have had when they were still operational may still work. The tunnels themselves do not see any traffic from any of the maintenance crew themselves. Although individuals have been known to live here, mostly individuals who were either former slaves, hiding from their masters. Or criminals, too afraid to make their living on the surface. Whatever the reason may be, the people that live their lives down here, live it primarily in solitude. Although it has been noted that some small groups of people live together down here, it is rare. As the only forms of nutrition down here are moss that grows on the rusted section of the piping and steel and the occasional flooded section creating a small ecosystem for fish. Occasionally, a food bar machine may still be operational down here or repaired by it's inhabitants. Allowing for more food variety. The tunnels themselves hold valuable scrap and potential contraband that can be scavenged and sold down in the depths for the people that live here.

The non-abandoned tunnels are normal maintenance tunnels as numerous and labyrinthine as their non-abandoned counterparts, they mostly have the same functions as their non-abandoned counterparts. But these tunnels are commonly walked through and actively maintained by maintenance crew. Additionally, the acting AI for the maintenance sections of the undercities deploy autonomous security measures against trespasses in the non-abandoned tunnels.
